p: beginning God created the heaven and: First of all, and before any creature was, God made heaven and earth out of nothing.
without form: As an unformed lump and without any creature in it: for the waters covered everything.
darkness was upon the face of: Darkness covered the deep waters, for the waters covered everything.
moved upon the face of the: He maintained this disordered mass by his secret power.
light: The light was made before either Sun or Moon was created: therefore we must not attribute that to the creatures that are God's instruments, which only belong to God.
under the firmament from the waters: As the sea and rivers, from those waters that are in the clouds, which are upheld by God's power, least they should overwhelm the world.
Heaven: That is, the region of the air, and all that is above us.
Let the earth bring forth grass: So that we see it is the only the power of God's word that makes the earth fruitful, which naturally is barren.

saw that it was good: This sentence is often repeated, to signify that God made all his creatures to serve for his glory and for the profit of man: but because of sin they were cursed, yet the elect, by Christ are restored, and serve to their wealth.
lights in the firmament of the: By the lights be means the sun, the moon, and the stars.
divide the day from the night: Which is the artificial day, from the sun rising, to the going down.
signs: Of things belonging to natural and political orders and seasons.
lights: That is, the sun and the moon, and here he speaks as man judges by his eye: for else the moon is less than the planet Saturn.
rule the day: To give it sufficient light, as instruments appointed for the same, to serve man's purposes.
moving creature that hath life: As fish and worms which slide, swim or creep.

waters brought forth abundantly: The fish and fowls had both one beginning, in which we see that nature gives place to God's will, in that the one sort is made to fly about in the air, and the other to swim beneath in the water.
blessed them: That is, by the virtue of his word he gave power to his creatures to reproduce.

Let us make man in our: God commanded the water and the earth to bring forth other creatures: but of man he says, "Let us make..." signifying that God takes counsel with his wisdom and virtue purposing to make an excellent work above all the rest of his creation.

image: This image and likeness of God in man is expounded in Eph 4:24 where it is written that man was created after God in righteousness and true holiness meaning by these two words, all perfection, as wisdom, truth, innocency, power, etc.
blessed them: The propagation.
every herb bearing seed: God's great.
